name: STM32L011F4P6TR
title: STM32L011x3/x4 ultra-low-power Arm Cortex-M0+ microcontrollers, 32 MHz, 8 or 16 Kbytes Flash, 2 Kbytes SRAM, 512 bytes EEPROM
summary: An access-line ultra-low-power microcontroller family built on a Cortex-M0+ core clocked from 32 kHz up to 32 MHz, with 8 or 16 Kbytes of ECC Flash, 2 Kbytes of SRAM and 512 bytes of ECC data EEPROM. It carries a 12-bit 1.14 Msps ADC with up to 10 external channels and oversampling to 16 bits, two low-power comparators, TIM2, TIM21, a low-power timer, an RTC, one USART, one LPUART, one SPI and one I2C, and runs from 1.65 V to 3.6 V with Standby down to 0.23 µA. Packages run from TSSOP14 to LQFP32. STM32L011F4P6TR is the 16 Kbyte TSSOP20 part with 16 I/Os, BOR enabled (1.8 V to 3.6 V), rated -40 °C to 85 °C, on tape and reel.
key_figures: Arm Cortex-M0+, 32 kHz to 32 MHz, 0.95 DMIPS/MHz
8 or 16 Kbytes Flash (ECC), 2 Kbytes SRAM, 512 bytes data EEPROM (ECC), 20-byte backup registers
1.8 V to 3.6 V with BOR, 1.65 V to 3.6 V without BOR
0.29 µA Stop, 0.54 µA Stop with RTC, 0.23 µA Standby
12-bit, 1.14 Msps, up to 10 external channels, down to 1.65 V
up to 28 fast I/Os, 23 of them 5 V tolerant (16 on TSSOP20)
HSI16 16 MHz ±1 %, MSI 65 kHz to 4.2 MHz, LSI 37 kHz

circuits.title: Power supply scheme
circuits.description: The digital supply VDD takes one 100 nF per VDD pin plus one 10 µF capacitor to VSS; the analog supply VDDA takes 100 nF plus 1 µF to ground. VDDA feeds the ADC, the RC oscillators, the PLL and the comparators; VDD feeds the I/Os and the core regulator. VDDA comes from the same source as VDD, within 300 mV of it. TSSOP20 has one VDD and one VDDA pin and VSSA is bonded to VSS inside.
notes: On TSSOP14, VDDA is joined to VDD inside the package and the VDDA capacitors go on the shared pin.

circuits.title: 32.768 kHz crystal on the LSE oscillator
circuits.description: A 32.768 kHz crystal or ceramic resonator between OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT, with load capacitor CL1 from OSC32_IN to ground and CL2 from OSC32_OUT to ground, clocks the RTC. The amplifier's drive is set in software by LSEDRV[1:0]. No resistor may be fitted across the crystal. A resonator with built-in capacitors replaces the crystal and both capacitors. Crystal and capacitors sit as close to the pins as possible.
notes: CL1 and CL2 follow from the crystal's load capacitance; ST application note AN2867 covers the choice.

circuits.title: Recommended NRST pin protection
circuits.description: A 0.1 µF capacitor from NRST to ground, placed as close to the chip as possible, guards against stray resets, and a push-button sits from NRST to ground. The pull-up RPU (25 kΩ to 65 kΩ) and a pulse filter are inside the chip. Whatever drives NRST has to pull it below VIL(NRST) max, or the reset is not seen.

circuits.title: Typical connection using the ADC
circuits.description: A source VAIN drives an analog input AINx through its output resistance RAIN; the pad and board add Cparasitic to ground, about 7 pF of it the pad. Inside, the pin has clamp diodes to VDDA and ground, ±50 nA leakage, and the sampling switch RADC (1 kΩ max) into CADC (8 pF max). RAIN stays under the limit of the RAIN equation and table for the sampling time chosen; a large Cparasitic costs accuracy, which a lower fADC wins back.

operation.text: Arm Cortex-M0+ with a two-stage pipeline and a single-cycle multiplier, 0.95 DMIPS/MHz, clocked up to 32 MHz. The NVIC takes up to 32 maskable interrupts at 4 priority levels, plus the NMI. Memory is 8 or 16 Kbytes of Flash and 512 bytes of data EEPROM, both with ECC, 2 Kbytes of SRAM at zero wait states, and an information block of 32 option bytes plus 4 Kbytes of system memory holding the bootloader. A 96-bit unique ID is present.

Option bytes set write protection in 4 Kbyte sectors and readout protection in three levels: level 0 open; level 1 blocks Flash reads and writes while a debugger is attached or the part boots from RAM; level 2 protects the whole chip from readout, with the SWD port and boot from RAM disabled.

The core regulator output is set by the frequency in use. Range 1 (VCORE 1.8 V) needs VDD 1.71 V to 3.6 V and allows up to 32 MHz; range 2 (1.5 V) allows 16 MHz and range 3 (1.2 V) 4.2 MHz, both over the full VDD range. Flash needs one wait state above 16 MHz in range 1, above 8 MHz in range 2, and none in range 3. Going up in frequency, each step is less than four times the last, with 5 µs between steps. Below VDD 1.71 V only ranges 2 and 3 work and the ADC runs at up to 570 ksps.

Sleep stops only the CPU, about 1 mA at 16 MHz with peripherals off. Low-power run runs from the MSI at up to 131 kHz with the regulator in low-power mode; low-power sleep adds Sleep to that. Stop keeps RAM and registers, stops every clock in the core domain and turns off PLL, MSI, HSI and HSE; the LSE or LSI may keep the RTC running. Any EXTI line wakes it in about 3.5 µs to 5 µs: any GPIO, the PVD, either comparator (with VREFINT on), the RTC, or USART, I2C, LPUART and LPTIM events. Standby turns the core domain off; RAM and registers are lost apart from the wakeup logic, IWDG, RTC, LSI, LSE and RCC_CSR. It ends on NRST, an IWDG reset, a rising edge on a WKUP pin, or an RTC alarm, tamper, timestamp or wakeup event, in about 60 µs. Entering Stop or Standby does not stop the RTC, the IWDG or their clocks.

VDD (1.65 V to 3.6 V) feeds the I/Os and the regulator. VDDA (1.65 V to 3.6 V) feeds the ADC, reset blocks, RC oscillators and PLL, and is tied to VDD, with VSSA tied to VSS; on TSSOP14 VDDA is bonded to VDD inside. Every supply and ground pin is connected.

A POR/PDR holds the chip in reset below about 1.5 V with no external circuit. Two versions exist: with the BOR active at power-on the part works from 1.8 V to 3.6 V and starts correctly whatever the ramp below 1.8 V; the D version without BOR works from 1.65 V, and its supply then has to reach 1.65 V within 1 ms of leaving the POR zone. After power-up the option bytes can change the BOR threshold (five levels, 1.8 V to 3 V) or turn the BOR off for good, which lowers VDD min to 1.65 V on either version. Start-up takes about 3.3 ms with the BOR active at power-on and about 1 ms without. VREFINT can be switched off in Stop to save current.

The PVD compares VDD/VDDA with one of seven software-chosen thresholds from 1.85 V to 3.05 V in steps of about 200 mV, and can interrupt on the supply falling below the threshold, rising above it, or both.
The regulator runs in main mode in Run, in low-power mode in Stop and in both low-power run and sleep, and is off (high impedance) in Standby, where only the standby circuitry keeps power.

At start-up the BOOT0 pin and the nBOOT0, nBOOT1 and nBOOT_SEL option bits pick boot from Flash, from system memory or from RAM. The system-memory bootloader reprograms Flash over SPI1 (PA4, PA5, PA6, PA7; on TSSOP14 PA4, PA7, PA13, PA14) or USART2 (PA2, PA3 and PA9, PA10). A blank part always starts the bootloader because of the empty check. BOOT0 shares its pin with PB9, an input only; with nBOOT_SEL cleared the pin is sampled on the rising edge of NRST and then reads as PB9. ST application note AN2606 covers the bootloader.

SYSCLK comes from an external clock of 0 to 32 MHz on CK_IN (HSE bypass; there is no HSE crystal oscillator), the 16 MHz HSI RC, or the MSI RC at one of 65 kHz, 131 kHz, 262 kHz, 524 kHz, 1.05 MHz, 2.1 MHz or 4.2 MHz; HSE and HSI can feed the PLL. With an LSE present the MSI can be trimmed to ±0.5 %. The RTC runs from the 32.768 kHz LSE crystal, the 37 kHz LSI (which also clocks the IWDG and can be measured against the HSI), or the HSE. After reset the part runs from the MSI at 2 MHz. A clock security system watches the LSE (not the HSE) and raises an interrupt or wakeup if it fails. MCO puts an internal clock out on a pin. AHB and both APB buses run up to 32 MHz.

The RTC is a BCD calendar with subseconds, two alarms and a periodic wakeup, all able to wake the part from Stop and Standby. It corrects for month length and leap years, takes a 50 Hz or 60 Hz reference input, has 1 ppm digital calibration and shift correction of 1 to 32767 clock pulses, two tamper pins with filters and a timestamp input, each able to wake the part. Five 32-bit backup registers (20 bytes) keep their contents in Standby and through a system reset. The RTC runs from a 32.768 kHz crystal, a resonator or oscillator, the LSI or the HSE.

Each GPIO is an output (push-pull or open-drain), an input (floating, pull-up or pull-down) or an alternate function, with four output speed settings. All are high-current capable. The alternate function setup can be locked. The I/O bus toggles at up to 32 MHz. Every I/O is a floating input during and after reset. FT and FTf pins take up to 5.5 V (5.2 V below VDD 2.0 V) with their pull resistors off; TC and TTa pins stay within VDD + 0.3 V. FTf pins sink 20 mA for I2C Fast-mode Plus. Pins sink or source ±8 mA at standard levels and ±15 mA with relaxed levels, within the package total.

26 edge detector lines: 16 configurable lines shared by the GPIOs and 10 lines for the PVD, RTC, USART, I2C, LPUART, LPTIM and comparator events. Each line triggers on rising, falling or both edges and is masked on its own; it catches pulses shorter than an APB2 clock period.
Five channels move data between memory and peripherals or from memory to memory, with circular buffers, for SPI, I2C, USART, LPUART, the timers and the ADC.

A 12-bit successive-approximation ADC with up to 10 external channels plus the temperature sensor (ADC_IN18) and VREFINT (ADC_IN17). PA0, PA4 and PA5 are fast channels; the others are standard channels with an extra protection resistance. It converts single-shot or in scan mode at up to 1.14 Msps whatever the CPU clock, draws about 25 µA at 10 ksps and 200 µA at 1 Msps, and powers down between conversions. A hardware oversampler of up to 256 samples gives 16-bit results. An analog watchdog flags conversions outside set thresholds, and timer events can start conversions. It works down to VDDA 1.65 V. A calibration after each power-up is advised. There is no VREF+ pin: VDDA is the reference, and VREFINT measures it.

The sensor's output is linear with temperature; its offset varies from part to part, so uncalibrated it suits only measuring changes. Each part carries a factory reading at 130 °C (TS_CAL2) in system memory. VREFINT, the bandgap for the ADC and comparators, is measured at 3 V and 25 °C for each part and stored as VREFINT_CAL. VREFINT is available on VREF_OUT (PB0 or PB1) through a buffer driving 1 µA typical.

Two comparators share bias and reference. COMP1 is the ultra-low-power one (160 nA typ); COMP2 is rail-to-rail with fast and slow modes. The threshold is an I/O pin, VREFINT, or for COMP2 1/4, 1/2 or 3/4 of VREFINT. Both wake the part from Stop and can pair as a window comparator, and their outputs can drive timer inputs.

TIM2 is a 16-bit up/down timer with four capture/compare channels, DMA, quadrature encoder and Hall sensor inputs. TIM21 is a 16-bit up/down timer with two channels, and can run from the LSE as a timebase apart from the CPU clock; the two link for synchronisation. LPTIM1 is a 16-bit timer that runs in Stop from the LSE, LSI or an external clock, with PWM, one-shot, encoder and glitch filter, and wakes the part. SysTick is a 24-bit down-counter. The IWDG (12-bit, 37 kHz LSI) runs in Stop and Standby and can be started in hardware by option byte; the WWDG (7-bit) runs from the main clock with an early warning interrupt. Counters can freeze in debug.

I2C1 runs Standard mode (100 kbit/s), Fast mode (400 kbit/s) and Fast-mode Plus (1 Mbit/s, 20 mA drive on FTf pins), master or slave, 7-bit and 10-bit addressing with two addresses. It supports SMBus 2.0 and PMBus 1.1, has its own clock domain and wakes the part from Stop on address match (not with the digital filter on). SDA and SCL are not true open-drain: the PMOS to VDD is switched off but still there. The analog filter meets I2C timing only for Fast-mode Plus at VDD 2.7 V to 3.6 V in range 1, and Fast mode at VDD 2 V to 3.6 V in range 1 or 2, or below 2 V with under 200 pF load; elsewhere the digital filter is used instead. Standard mode needs no spike filter.

USART2 runs to 4 Mbit/s with CTS/RTS, RS485 driver enable, multiprocessor and single-wire half-duplex modes, ISO 7816 smartcard (T=0) and IrDA SIR. LPUART1 has its own clock domain and wakes the part from Stop at up to 46 kbaud on a start bit, any frame or a set frame; from the LSE alone it runs up to 9600 baud.
SPI1 runs master or slave at up to 16 Mbit/s, full or half duplex, 8-bit or 16-bit frames, with a 3-bit prescaler, hardware CRC and TI mode; no I2S.
A CRC unit with configurable polynomial and size checks Flash or data integrity. Debug is Arm serial wire (SWD) on PA13 (SWDIO) and PA14 (SWCLK).

Voltages refer to VSS. Minimum and maximum figures hold over the worst ambient, supply and frequency and are production tested at 25 °C and TA max, unless marked as from characterization (mean ±3σ). Typical figures are at 25 °C and VDD = 3.6 V and are not tested; typical ADC accuracy covers 95 % of parts (mean ±2σ). Pins are loaded with 50 pF for pin measurements.

Run-mode currents use code equivalent to Dhrystone 2.1 unless stated. All I/Os are in analog input mode, peripherals off unless named, Flash wait states and prefetch set for best speed, fAPB1 = fAPB2, PLL fed from HSI16 or a 16 MHz HSE bypass clock on CK_IN. Maximum figures are at VDD = VDDA = 3.6 V, typical at 3.0 V.
Waking from Stop draws on average 1 mA on the HSI down to 0.1 mA on the MSI at 65 kHz; waking from Standby draws 0.5 mA with fast wakeup and 0.12 mA without.

The LSE crystal and its load capacitors sit right at OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT to limit distortion and start-up time. Start-up time depends strongly on the crystal; a low-drive crystal in a high-drive mode starts faster.

EMC was characterized on the component with a simple application. Software should catch a corrupted program counter, an unexpected reset and corrupted control data; forcing NRST or the oscillator pins low for 1 second reproduces most of these faults, and ESD stress on the part completes the trial (ST application note AN1015).

Injection into I/Os is to be avoided in normal use. Negative current into a standard analog input upsets conversions on other inputs; a Schottky diode from pin to ground is advised on analog pins that may inject negative current. FT pins and BOOT0 accept no positive injection.
The current sourced by all I/Os plus the run current from VDD stays within ΣIVDD, and the current sunk by all I/Os plus the run current into VSS stays within ΣIVSS.

Junction temperature is TA plus PD × ΘJA, PD being internal power IDD × VDD plus the output drivers' dissipation. ΘJA is 74 °C/W for TSSOP20, measured per JEDEC JESD51-2 in still air. TJ stays within 105 °C (suffix 6), 125 °C (suffix 7) or 130 °C (suffix 3).

UFQFPN32 has an exposed pad underneath, best soldered to board ground. On TSSOP20, body length D excludes mold flash, protrusions and gate burrs of up to 0.15 mm per side, and body width E1 excludes interlead flash of up to 0.25 mm per side. On WLCSP25, A3 is the back side coating and the bump diameter b is measured at its widest, parallel to datum Z. All packages are ECOPACK2.
